items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: So then it happens that with my good friend Pee Wee Irwin and we were going out to play a jazz gig out in Pennsylvania

ctx.x: So it was like you’ve seen the writing on the wall?

I didn’t. I was stubborn. I was very stubborn. And I said oh it will never happen. Those guys can’t play. Listen to that, they can’t even play an ending. Every record fades out. They can’t even play an ending. None of them can play. But everybody said hey Sonny, you’ve got to get onto this. So okay. So then it happens that with my good friend Pee Wee Irwin and we were going out to play a jazz gig out in Pennsylvania and I’m driving and Pee Wee and I are chatting. Now this is not to be derogatory to any specific…

I don’t care what style it is, if you’re going to play Latin if you’re playing lousy I’m going to know it. But some of these guys are really good but the music, oh God, terrible. That’s only my opinion folks.
